chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithammi, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a medicine kneaded with wine, can we apply it in the eyes from it? So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'What Allah, Mighty and Majestic, placed in what He forbade is not a healing.'
ai.seo_question: Is medicine mixed with wine permissible for use if applied externally?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a general principle that the intrinsic prohibition of a substance negates its medicinal utility, even when applied externally as kohl. This hadith is central to the Shia juristic debate on whether the impurity (najāsah) of wine renders it non-medicinal, contrasting with views that focus solely on consumption. It underscores the concept that divine wisdom in prohibition extends to the substance's essence, not just its mode of intake.
